t: The death of Pasquale Falco, 1 October 1834
c: Arienzo civil death register 1834, page 236, act no. 69 (Archivio di Stato di Caserta, via Antenati). Names him husband of Chiara Rivetti and son of the late Matteo Falco and the late Francesca Crisci. Found by reading the volume line by line.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1834, atto 69, p. 236 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14336, img 43)

t: The birth of Raffaele Falco — 10 May 1818
c: Act no. 47, foglio 149. Vincenzo Falco, twenty-seven, a contadino of strada Camellara, declares a son born that afternoon to himself and Andreana Crisci, his lawful wife, aged twenty — and the child is named Raffaele. Generation four of this line, previously known only as “1818” from a parish baptism.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile napoleonico e della restaurazione, Nati 1818, atto 47, f. 149 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14415, img 41).

t: An earlier Raffaele Falco — 25 April 1816
c: Act no. 56. Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci, of strada Camellara, name a son Raffaele — two years before they named another son Raffaele on 10 May 1818. Ordinarily that means the first child died. Which of the two is generation four of this line is now an open question. The two acts also give irreconcilable ages: Vincenzo thirty-five here and twenty-seven two years later.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile napoleonico e della restaurazione, Nati 1816, atto 56 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14413, img 29).

t: A second Giuseppe Falco — 25 November 1816
c: Act no. 116. Giuseppe Falco, thirty-six, a massaro di campo of strada COSTA, declares a son born at four in the night to himself and Gelsomina Vigliotta, thirty-two, and names him Domenico. This is not the Giuseppe Falco of strada Camellara, a contadino married to Antonia di Guida, who was also thirty-six two years later — two men of one name and near-identical age in the same small town.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile napoleonico e della restaurazione, Nati 1816, atto 116 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14413, img 59).

t: Donna Francesca Rivetti — 26 January 1816
c: Act no. 12. «Donna Francesca Rivetti, figlia del fu Don Nicola, e Donn'Anna Quotolo, moglie di Don Claudio Cimmino.» Chiara Rivetti — who married Pasquale Falco — is called in 1843 «filia quondam Nicolai et Anna». The same two forenames. If the two women are sisters, this gives Chiara's mother a surname and makes the Rivetti gentry. That is a lead, not a finding: Nicola and Anna are among the commonest names in the register, and Chiara married a contadino where Francesca married a Don.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1816, atto 12 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14318, img 7).

t: Giuseppe Falco of strada Camellara — 7 June 1818
c: Act no. 57, foglio 154. Giuseppe Falco, thirty-six, a contadino of strada Camellara, declares a daughter born to himself and Antonia di Guida, thirty, and names her Maddalena. The parish marriage record calls this Giuseppe «filium Matthei, e Franciscae Crisci» — so this is Pasquale's own brother, living on the same street, four weeks after his nephew Raffaele was born on it.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile napoleonico e della restaurazione, Nati 1818, atto 57, f. 154 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14415, img 46).

t: Pasquale Falco, aged three — 22 February 1833
c: Arienzo civil death register 1833, act no. 16. Son of Vincenzo Falco and Andreana Crisci, of strada Camellara. His grandfather Pasquale was still alive; a second child of the same name would be born and die in December 1834.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1833, atto 16 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14335, img 9)

t: Rosa Falco, forty-two — 16 October 1830
c: Act no. 53, page 89. «Rosa Falco, d'anni quarantadue, moglie di Carlantonio Morgillo … figlia di Matteo Falco, defunto … e di Francesca Crisci, defunta.» She is Pasquale's sister, and this names the line's founding couple a second time, from a different child and four years before Pasquale's own death act.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1830, atto 53, p. 89 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14332, img 36).

t: Anna Falco, thirteen months — 4 May 1831
c: Act no. 33, page 67. Daughter of Michelangelo Falco and Mariantonia Vigliotta, of strada Camellara. The second declarant is Vincenzo Falco, thirty-eight — generation three of this line — described not as a neighbour but as «parente della defunta», a kinsman. It is the first record joining the direct line to another Falco household on that street.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1831, atto 33, p. 67 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14333, img 19).

t: Giovanna Falco, aged seventy — 13 May 1832
c: Act no. 32. She was born about 1762, five years before Pasquale, and her father was a different Michele Falco, married to Vincenza Esposito. The record establishes a second peasant Falco household at Arienzo in the founding generation.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1832, atto 32 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14334, img 20)

t: Carmina Falco, six months — 19 December 1832
c: Act no. 80, page 145. Daughter of Francesco Falco and Raffaela Falco, of strada Camellara — a Falco married to a Falco. Both declarants were neighbours from the same street.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1832, atto 80, p. 145 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14334, img 48)

t: The reverse of the certificate — an inscription of 1948
c: The back of a family document, inscribed «li 14 Dicembre 1948 — Giordano Angelo». Who Giordano Angelo was, and what he had to do with this family, is not established. Recorded because it is written on one of the family's own papers.
cite: Family papers, from the family's own scans.

t: Croce al Merito di Guerra — Angelo Zampiello, 1938
c: Ministero dell'Africa Italiana. The War Merit Cross, conferred by decree of 14 September 1938 on «all'operaio ZAMPIELLO ANGELO di Tommaso» — the workman Angelo Zampiello, son of Tommaso. The decree cited extends the cross to personnel who took part in military operations in East Africa from 3 October 1935, the day Italy invaded Ethiopia. Order number 18745; Rome, 24 September 1938, Anno XVI.
cite: Family papers, from the family's own scans. Ministero dell'Africa Italiana, n. d'ordine 18745.

t: Birth extract of Francesca Zampiello, Arpaia
c: Comune di Arpaia, provincia di Benevento — «Estratto dell'atto di nascita n. 20». Born 27 April 1928 at Arpaia: ZAMPIELLO FRANCESCA, daughter of ZAMPIELLO ANGELO and FERRARA GIUSEPPA. A certified photocopy issued in 2003. This is the document behind the birth date the family carried, and it names both parents.
cite: Comune di Arpaia (BN), estratto dell'atto di nascita n. 20, issued 2003.

t: Angelo Zampiello and Giuseppa Ferrara
c: A hand-tinted paired portrait: Giuseppa Ferrara at the left, Angelo Zampiello at the right.

t: Angelo Zampiello — the memorial card
c: A memorial card, photographed on a crocheted cloth and rotated upright here: «ZAMPIELLO ANGELO — Nato il 31 agosto 1895 — Morto il 25 aprile 1972». It corroborates both dates from the family's own paper.

t: An elderly couple — identification uncertain
c: Two oval portraits mounted on card. The same photograph appears twice in the family scans, filed once under Angelo Zampiello and once under Carminantonio Falco. This archive cannot tell which couple it is, and says so rather than choosing.

t: Filomena Annecchino
c: Born 10 April 1897. Photographed in old age in a headscarf and crocheted shawl. The family remembers her hiding in a tree above her husband and his mistress.

t: Marriage extract — Falco and Zampiello, Arpaia, 1955
c: Comune di Arpaia — «Estratto dell'atto di matrimonio n. 1». FALCO CARMINE, born 8 June 1930, married ZAMPIELLO FRANCESCA, born 27 April 1928, on 15 January 1955. Registered at Arpaia — not, as this archive previously said, at Benevento.
cite: Comune di Arpaia (BN), estratto dell'atto di matrimonio n. 1, issued 2003.

t: The cemetery index, 2 January 1991
c: Page 64 of a burial index. Four Falcos: Carmine Antonio and Filomena on page 504, Caterina and Raffaele on page 284. It was this scrap that led to the Nudgee burial registers, and from there to the Brisbane immigration files.

t: The death of Crescenzo Rivetti, 1 December 1816 — and the first sighting of Gioacchino Falco
c: Arienzo civil death register 1816, act no. 76. Two Falco of strada Camellara declare it and are described as «parenti del defunto» — kin of the dead man: Gioacchino Falco, 36, and Giuseppe Falco, 32, both massari di campagna. The dead man is «Crescenzo Rivetti figlio del fu Pasquale Rivetti e di Giovanna Perrotta, marito di Angela Falco». No age is given for him. The act therefore records a Falco marriage this archive did not have, and a Falco head — Gioacchino — it had never met.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1816, atto 76 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14318, img 42, left column)

t: The death of Maria Falco, 24 July 1817
c: Arienzo civil death register 1817. «Maria Falco figlia delli fu Giuseppe Falco e Rosa Sossi, vedova di Francesco Quotolo». Declared by Giuseppe Quotolo, 65, massaro di campagna of strada Maddalena, and Aniello Diglio, 45, contadino — her late husband's kin. Both her parents were already dead. This is a Falco couple the archive had never met, and it is not the Giuseppe Falco of strada Camellara, who was alive in 1818.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1817 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14319, img 34, left column)

t: The death of Angelo Andrea di Guida, 21 October 1817
c: Arienzo civil death register 1817. «Angelo Andrea di Guida figlio di Giuseppe di Guida e Michedalena Rivetti, marito di Teresa Vigliotta», declared by Francesco Quotolo, 33, and Pietro Quotolo, 30, both massari di campagna of strada Maddalena. One act, three of the surnames the Falco married into: di Guida (Giuseppe Falco's wife Antonia), Rivetti (Pasquale Falco's wife Chiara) and Vigliotta (Michelangelo's wife Mariantonia and the strada Costa Giuseppe's wife Gelsomina). Whether Antonia di Guida belongs to this house is a lead, not a finding.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1817 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14319, img 59, right column)

t: The burial of the first Raffaele Falco, 28 October 1817 — the act that settled generation four
c: Arienzo civil death register 1817. «Raffaele Falco figlio di Vincenzo Falco, e d'Andreana Crisci», dead at seven in the morning, aged about eighteen months. Vincenzo and Andreana had registered a son Raffaele on 25 April 1816 and another on 10 May 1818; until this act was found, the archive could not say which was the ancestor and carried generation four as disputed. This is the first one's burial. The declarants are Sabato Vassallo, 26, sportellaro of strada Porta di Sopra, and GIUSEPPE FALCO, 37, massaro di campagna of strada Camellara — the two of them recorded as «parenti», kin.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1817 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14319, img 61, left column)

t: The death of Angela «Lella» Majone, 27 February 1818 — a second Falco marriage
c: Arienzo civil death register, bound at the end of the 1817 volume. «Angela, seu Lella Majone, figlia delli fu Nicola Majone, e MARIA FALCO, moglie di Giuseppe Sossi». Both her parents were dead. A Falco woman married into the Majone — and whether she is the Maria Falco buried seven months earlier, widow of Francesco Quotolo, is deliberately left open: one woman twice widowed fits the dates, and so do two women of the same name.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14319, img 88, right column)

t: Giuseppe Falco of strada Camellara, declaring, 8 May 1818
c: Arienzo civil death register 1818. «Domenico Balletta, di anni quaranta, sartore, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara, e di GIUSEPPE FALCO, di anni trentasei, contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Camellara, vicini» — the two of them declaring a neighbour's death. Four weeks later the birth act of Giuseppe's daughter Maddalena gives exactly the same age, trade and street. Five sightings of this man now exist across nineteen months, and this is the one that proves they are a single person rather than two Giuseppe Falco on one street.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1818 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14320, img 24, left column)

t: Orazio Morgillo of strada Travo, 6 July 1818
c: Arienzo civil death register 1818. «Angelo Morgillo fu Simone, di anni cinquanta, contadino, strada Travo, e di ORAZIO MORGILLO, di anni ventisei, contadino, strada Travo» declaring the death of Pasquale Morgillo, «figlio di Giuseppe Morgillo, e GELSOMINA RIVETTI». Generation four of this line married Angela Rosa Morgillo, recorded as a daughter of an Orazio; an Orazio Morgillo aged twenty-six in 1818 is the right age for her father. He is also the first Orazio Morgillo this archive has found in any record. It is a lead and not a link — Angela Rosa was born at San Felice, not Arienzo.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1818 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14320, img 31, right column)

t: Carlantonio Morgillo declaring, 3 August 1818 — and a second Carlantonio
c: Arienzo civil death register 1818. «Carlantonio Morgillo, di anni trentatre, contadino, domiciliato in questo comune, strada Maddalena» declares, as «vicino, parente», the death of «Giuditta Morgillo figlia delli fu CARLANTONIO MORGILLO, e MANILIA RIVETTI, vedova di Giuseppe Gimbardo». The declarant is Rosa Falco's husband — Pasquale Falco's brother-in-law. The dead woman's father is a different, older Carlantonio Morgillo. If the declarant is Giuditta's brother, as the word «parente» hints, this act names his parents; the register does not say so, and this archive does not assert it.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1818 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14320, img 38, right column)

t: Angelandrea Rivetti, daughter of Angela Falco — 12 February 1819
c: Arienzo civil death register 1819. «Angelandrea Rivetti figlia del fu CRESCENZO RIVETTI, ed ANGELA FALCO». Crescenzo died on 1 December 1816, in an act declared by Gioacchino Falco and Giuseppe Falco as «parenti del defunto» — the act that first told this archive a Falco had married a Rivetti. This is their daughter, dead two years later, and the second record anywhere to name Angela Falco. She is written without «fu», so she was still alive.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1819 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14321, img 5, left column)

t: Domenico Falco, 15 March 1819
c: Arienzo civil death register 1819. «Domenico Falco figlio di Giuseppe Falco, e Gelsomina Vigliotta», dead at twelve o'clock. He was born on 25 November 1816 and was two years and four months old. His sister Rosaria died the same day, eleven hours later.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1819 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14321, img 8)

t: Rosaria Falco, 15 March 1819 — the same day as her brother
c: Arienzo civil death register 1819. «Rosaria Falco figlia di Giuseppe Falco, e Gelsomina Vigliotta», dead at twenty-three hours on 15 March 1819 — the same day her brother Domenico died at noon. Two children of one house in a single day. No birth act has been found for Rosaria: she is not in the Arienzo birth registers of 1816, 1817 or 1818, so she was born before them.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1819 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14321, img 8)

t: Fortunato Crisci, two days old — and the marriage of Arcangelo Crisci and Anna Falco
c: Arienzo civil death register 1820, act 5. «È morto nella sua propria casa FORTUNATO CRISCI di giorni due, nato in Arienzo, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, figlio di ARCANGELO CRISCI, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, E DI ANNA FALCO, domiciliata ivi.» Declared by Andrea Crisci, 60, and Marcello Crisci, 25, both of strada Camellara. This archive had the marriage of Arcangelo Crisci and Anna Falco only at second hand; here it is in a civil act, with the household placed on the family's own street. The 1820 form is far fuller than those of 1816-19: it gives the dead person's age, birthplace, trade and address, both parents with their trades, and each declarant's relationship to the deceased.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1820, atto 5 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14322, img 5, right column)

t: Anna Falco, 23 August 1820 — a daughter of Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti
c: Arienzo civil death register 1820, atto 47. «È morta nella sua propria casa ANNA FALCO di anni venticinque, moglie di ARCANGELO CRISCI, nata in Arienzo, di professione Contadina, domiciliata ivi strada Camellara, FIGLIA DI PASQUALE FALCO, di professione Contadino, domiciliato ivi strada Camellara, E DI CHIARA RIVETTI, domiciliata ivi.» A child of the direct line's generation two that this archive did not have, and a sister of Vincenzo Falco. Both her parents are named WITHOUT «fu», so Pasquale Falco and Chiara Rivetti were both alive and on strada Camellara in August 1820 — the only civil sighting of Pasquale between his marriage and his death in 1834. Declared by Giuseppe Martone, 40, and Domenico Martone, 36, neighbours on the same street.
cite: Arienzo, Stato civile della restaurazione, Morti 1820, atto 47 — Archivio di Stato di Caserta (Antenati an_ua14322, img 26, right column)
